project.name: Pytyliki IRON CORE
project.purpose: A processor and hardware-engineering platform covering bit-level representation, ISA and CPU models, memory and device control, timing, digital/analog simulation, compilation integration and evidence-based verification.

baseline.current_product_boundary: The audited main branch is a C11 processor-systems workstation with read-only host discovery, bounded measurements, source diagnostics, memory utilities, numerical metrics, reference/simulated embedded models, and a merged capability-gated low-level C11 target contract. That target contract provides target descriptors, bounded non-overlapping memory maps, RAM/MMIO backend callbacks, capability checks, clock/power requests and a bounded IRQ registry tested with a fake backend. It does not ship a physical target backend, production kernel driver, complete typed hardware-language frontend, MMU, DMA engine or universal device map.

ownership.pytyliki: Owns processor/device profiles, hardware-domain APIs, native adapters, simulator orchestration, target evidence, diagnostics and qualification workflows.
ownership.reaper: Owns canonical language syntax, type/effect semantics, Span/SourceMap, typed IR, compiler passes and shared ABI/compiler contracts. Pytyliki must integrate these rather than fork them.
ownership.duck_os: Owns privileged process/device services, driver lifecycle, protected memory mapping, interrupt routing and OS-mediated hardware permissions.
ownership.board_backend: Owns exact SoC/board memory maps, startup/linker configuration, vendor HAL, electrical/process libraries and physical-design sign-off.
ownership.joint: Requires versioned contracts between Pytyliki, Reaper, Duck OS and/or a board-specific backend.

modes.effect: Produce an inert, bounded operation plan; perform no host or device mutation.
Execute only against an explicitly selected deterministic model.
Run static, formal, differential or conformance checks against supplied artifacts/models.
Use a named, explicitly configured target adapter with bounded non-privileged operations.
Perform narrowly scoped OS/driver/board operations only with explicit capabilities and trusted platform mediation.
Run external EDA flows against declared process/library data; physical sign-off requires external evidence.

maturity_levels.name: Language and contract foundation
maturity_levels.scope: Canonical Reaper syntax/IR contract, target descriptors, capability vocabulary and deterministic diagnostics.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Grammar, type/effect and target-profile conformance checks pass.

maturity_levels.name: Bit and machine representation
maturity_levels.scope: Bit vectors, exact layout, register model, ASM effects and ISA encoding/decoding.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Golden bit-layout, register and instruction vectors pass.

maturity_levels.name: Processor and microarchitecture
maturity_levels.scope: CPU topology plus configurable architectural and microarchitectural models.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Reference CPU model passes architectural fixtures and deterministic traces.

maturity_levels.name: Memory engineering
maturity_levels.scope: Address spaces, MMU, page tables, TLB, cache, atomics, DMA ownership.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Translation, memory-ordering and ownership model tests pass.

maturity_levels.name: Device and I/O engineering
maturity_levels.scope: Typed MMIO, bus/device models, IRQ and driver lifecycle adapters.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Simulator and target-specific device-contract tests pass.

maturity_levels.name: Execution and timing engineering
maturity_levels.scope: Execution contexts, scheduling models, clocks, cycle and latency evidence.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Replayable timing reports and context-safety checks pass.

maturity_levels.name: Digital and analog engineering
maturity_levels.scope: Logic, sequential circuits, clock domains, netlists, transistor/electrical models.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Reference circuit and timing analyses pass for declared libraries/models.

maturity_levels.name: Compiler and artifact engineering
maturity_levels.scope: Reaper lowering, ABI, assembler, object writer, linker, loader and no-runtime profiles.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Golden IR/object/relocation fixtures and reproducible-build checks pass.

maturity_levels.name: Verification and evidence engineering
maturity_levels.scope: Static/formal analysis, simulators, fault injection, hardware-in-loop and provenance.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Every capability status is tied to reproducible evidence and explicit test mode.

maturity_levels.name: Physical hardware engineering
maturity_levels.scope: Vendor/process libraries, physical design, DRC/LVS, PVT, fabricated-target qualification.
maturity_levels.acceptance_gate: Named physical implementation passes external EDA sign-off and board/silicon qualification.

rules.title: Exact representation
rules.requirement: Every scalar and aggregate has a defined size, alignment, bit representation, endianness and valid value range.
rules.acceptance: Compile-time layout reports and golden byte vectors agree with the declared target ABI.

rules.title: Parameterized bit vectors
rules.requirement: Provide bounded compile-time bit vectors of widths not limited to 8, 16, 32 or 64 bits.
rules.acceptance: Widths, slicing, concatenation, shifts and overflow behavior pass exhaustive tests for small widths and property tests for larger widths.

rules.title: Defined integer arithmetic
rules.requirement: Signedness, overflow, carry, borrow, saturation, division-by-zero and shift edge cases have explicit semantics.
rules.acceptance: Boundary tests match the language specification on every supported backend; no host-language undefined behavior leaks through.

rules.title: Floating-point representation
rules.requirement: Expose floating-point format, rounding mode, exceptional values and bit-level reinterpretation explicitly.
rules.acceptance: Tests cover NaN payloads, infinities, signed zero, subnormals and target-specific format constraints.

rules.title: Aggregate and bit-field layout
rules.requirement: Specify field ordering, packing, padding, alignment and ABI layout without implicit compiler guesses.
rules.acceptance: A layout inspector emits offsets and byte images that match ABI conformance fixtures.

rules.title: Aliasing and object lifetime
rules.requirement: Define when storage may be viewed through multiple types and how object lifetime begins and ends.
rules.acceptance: Static analysis rejects invalid aliasing/lifetime transitions or requires an explicit unsafe contract.

rules.title: Endianness as a type property
rules.requirement: Make byte order explicit at serialization, MMIO and cross-target boundaries.
rules.acceptance: Big- and little-endian golden vectors round-trip without host-endian assumptions.

rules.title: Observable effects
rules.requirement: Represent memory, register, I/O, timing, synchronization and privilege effects in the type/effect model.
rules.acceptance: Effect reports identify all externally observable operations for each function and reject undeclared effects.

rules.title: Operation cost evidence
rules.requirement: Associate target-specific instruction, memory and latency estimates with operations without presenting estimates as guarantees.
rules.acceptance: Compiler reports separate static estimates from measured samples and carry target/provenance metadata.

rules.title: Formal semantics for constructs
rules.requirement: Specify grammar, type rules, evaluation order, effects, traps and observable behavior for every accepted construct.
rules.acceptance: Every language construct has normative semantics plus positive, negative and regression conformance tests.

rules.title: Bit-addressable operations
rules.requirement: Expose individual-bit read, write, test, set, clear, toggle, mask and field extraction primitives.
rules.acceptance: Property tests verify exact results for all bit positions and reject out-of-range indexes.

rules.title: Condition-code model
rules.requirement: Represent target condition flags and their producer/consumer semantics explicitly.
rules.acceptance: ISA fixtures verify flag writes, preservation and condition evaluation per instruction.

rules.title: Typed CPU registers
rules.requirement: Model general, vector, floating-point, control, debug and status registers as target-specific typed entities.
rules.acceptance: Register descriptors validate width, access class, architectural availability and privilege before a read or write plan.

rules.title: Privileged register access
rules.requirement: Separate user-accessible, privileged, debug-only and unavailable registers; never infer permission from register existence.
rules.acceptance: An unprivileged target rejects privileged operations before backend dispatch; tests assert no side effects.

rules.title: Inline assembly contract
rules.requirement: Support assembly blocks with declared inputs, outputs, clobbers, memory effects, control-flow effects and target constraints.
rules.acceptance: Compiler rejects incomplete clobber/effect declarations and preserves declared register constraints.

rules.title: Instruction decoding
rules.requirement: Decode supported machine encodings into typed instruction records with operands, length and feature requirements.
rules.acceptance: Round-trip and malformed-byte fixtures cover each supported encoding family; unknown encodings remain unknown.

rules.title: Instruction encoding
rules.requirement: Encode typed instructions while validating operand forms, feature gates and target-specific constraints.
rules.acceptance: Encoded bytes match published architectural fixtures and invalid operands are rejected.

rules.title: Feature versus OS-state gating
rules.requirement: Distinguish hardware-present ISA features from features enabled and usable under the current OS/runtime state.
rules.acceptance: Dispatch tests reject AVX/other stateful extensions when required OS-managed register state is unavailable.

rules.title: Instruction semantic metadata
rules.requirement: Maintain machine-readable instruction semantics including registers read/written, flags, memory, exceptions and serialization.
rules.acceptance: Each supported instruction descriptor has complete metadata checked against conformance fixtures.

rules.title: Machine-code image model
rules.requirement: Represent sections, symbols, relocations, entry points, permissions and architecture identity without executing the image.
rules.acceptance: Image validation rejects invalid bounds, overlaps, unsupported relocations and mismatched architecture tags.

rules.title: CPU topology model
rules.requirement: Represent packages, dies, clusters, cores, SMT threads, cache sharing and NUMA relations with provenance.
rules.acceptance: Topology validation rejects duplicate IDs and impossible parent relations; live inventory is distinguished from fixtures.

rules.title: Execution-unit models
rules.requirement: Model scalar integer, floating-point, vector, cryptographic and specialized execution resources.
rules.acceptance: A reference CPU model routes supported operations to declared units and reports unsupported operations explicitly.

rules.title: Pipeline stages
rules.requirement: Describe fetch, decode, rename, schedule, execute, memory and retirement stages with configurable latencies.
rules.acceptance: Cycle simulation produces deterministic stage traces for a documented microarchitecture fixture.

rules.title: Dependency and hazard analysis
rules.requirement: Track RAW, WAR and WAW dependencies, memory alias uncertainty and structural hazards.
rules.acceptance: Hazard tests demonstrate stalls, forwarding or rejection according to the selected model.

rules.title: Superscalar issue model
rules.requirement: Model issue width, queues, port pressure, reorder capacity and retirement limits.
rules.acceptance: Instruction traces obey configured throughput and resource constraints without claiming to reproduce undocumented silicon.

rules.title: Branch prediction model
rules.requirement: Support configurable predictors, history, target buffers, miss penalties and speculation boundaries.
rules.acceptance: Deterministic branch traces report prediction outcomes and modeled penalties.

rules.title: Speculation and side-channel model
rules.requirement: Represent speculative execution, transient state and observable timing channels for security analysis.
rules.acceptance: Security fixtures detect declared leakage patterns; simulation results are labeled model evidence, not proof of silicon behavior.

rules.title: Cache hierarchy and protocol model
rules.requirement: Describe cache levels, line size, associativity, replacement policy, inclusion and coherence protocol.
rules.acceptance: Cache-model tests validate hits, misses, evictions and protocol transitions against deterministic traces.

rules.title: Performance counter integration
rules.requirement: Read supported OS/performance-counter sources only through explicit provider adapters with units and permissions.
rules.acceptance: Counter records identify provider, event, scope, unit, multiplexing and uncertainty; unsupported events remain unavailable.

rules.title: Custom CPU and ISA descriptions
rules.requirement: Allow versioned processor models with register files, instructions, execution resources, memory model and exceptions.
rules.acceptance: A custom model passes model-schema validation and executes the shared architecture conformance suite.

rules.title: Typed address spaces
rules.requirement: Keep virtual, physical, bus, I/O-port and device addresses as distinct non-interchangeable types.
rules.acceptance: The type checker rejects implicit casts between address spaces; explicit checked conversions require a platform capability.

rules.title: Page-table representation
rules.requirement: Model page-table formats, levels, entries, permissions, page sizes and reserved bits per architecture.
rules.acceptance: Fixtures decode valid and invalid page tables and reject reserved-bit or alignment violations.

rules.title: MMU translation model
rules.requirement: Translate virtual addresses through a declared page-table root and architecture profile.
rules.acceptance: Translation tests cover permissions, page faults, large pages and address-width boundaries.

rules.title: TLB model and invalidation
rules.requirement: Represent TLB entries, address-space tags, invalidation scope and required ordering.
rules.acceptance: Tests distinguish local/global invalidation and reject unsupported invalidation semantics.

rules.title: Cache-maintenance correctness
rules.requirement: Describe cache clean, invalidate and clean-invalidate operations by architecture and memory region.
rules.acceptance: A backend must declare exact operation semantics; unsupported operations return unsupported, never a silent no-op.

rules.title: Coherence and ownership
rules.requirement: Model cache-line ownership, sharing, visibility and device/CPU coherency boundaries.
rules.acceptance: Concurrent CPU/device traces detect stale-data scenarios and require the correct synchronization sequence.

rules.title: Memory ordering model
rules.requirement: Provide explicit atomic orders and target mappings, including fences and device-ordering distinctions.
rules.acceptance: Litmus tests pass for declared guarantees on each backend; unsupported mappings are rejected.

rules.title: Placement and section control
rules.requirement: Place code/data/stack/heap/NOINIT sections into named memory regions with alignment and capacity constraints.
rules.acceptance: Linker-map checks prove every section fits its declared region and report slack/overflow.

rules.title: DMA buffers and IOMMU mappings
rules.requirement: Represent buffer direction, ownership, lifetime, pinning, mapping and IOMMU permissions explicitly.
rules.acceptance: State-machine tests reject use-after-unmap, CPU/device concurrent ownership and out-of-range descriptors.

rules.title: Memory-system diagnostics
rules.requirement: Inspect allocator bounds, fragmentation, locality, bandwidth, faults and address-translation evidence.
rules.acceptance: Reports identify sample source, method, target and uncertainty; simulated and live evidence are never mixed.

rules.title: Typed MMIO registers
rules.requirement: Represent device registers with width, access class, reset value, writable mask, endian and ordering requirements.
rules.acceptance: Register access validates mapping bounds, alignment, width, permission and reserved bits before touching the backend.

rules.title: Machine-readable register maps
rules.requirement: Import documented CMSIS-SVD, device-tree bindings or vendor register descriptions as versioned input.
rules.acceptance: Import is deterministic, records source/version and rejects overlapping or malformed register definitions.

rules.title: Bus protocol models
rules.requirement: Provide explicit models/adapters for PCIe, USB, I2C, SPI, UART and platform-specific interconnects.
rules.acceptance: Each adapter declares supported transactions, limits, timeouts and whether it is simulated or backed by a live OS service.

rules.title: Interrupt-controller integration
rules.requirement: Model vector tables, interrupt routing, masking, priorities, nesting and architecture-specific entry constraints.
rules.acceptance: Target tests validate vector bounds and priority rules; privileged registration is available only via a trusted OS/board backend.

rules.title: Clock and watchdog controls
rules.requirement: Inspect and, where explicitly supported, configure timers, clock sources and watchdogs through a board-specific HAL.
rules.acceptance: Every write requires an exact board/revision profile, capability, safe-state plan and simulator/target conformance test.

rules.title: Device discovery and identity
rules.requirement: Enumerate device IDs, topology, functions, resources and driver ownership from trusted platform interfaces.
rules.acceptance: Reports preserve provider provenance and distinguish absent, inaccessible and unsupported devices.

rules.title: Driver lifecycle contracts
rules.requirement: Specify probe, bind, start, quiesce, suspend, resume, unbind and failure states for device drivers.
rules.acceptance: State-machine tests ensure resources are acquired/released once and failed starts roll back safely.

rules.title: DMA engine descriptors
rules.requirement: Build and validate device-specific DMA descriptor rings and queue ownership through target adapters.
rules.acceptance: Descriptor validation checks alignment, bounds, chain termination, permissions and memory synchronization.

rules.title: Port-mapped I/O
rules.requirement: Support architecture-specific I/O port operations only when the target and privilege model expose them.
rules.acceptance: Compilation and execution are gated by architecture, OS permission and a dedicated backend; unsupported targets fail closed.

rules.title: Device failure and recovery
rules.requirement: Model bus faults, timeouts, device reset, link retraining and recovery checkpoints.
rules.acceptance: Fault-injection tests prove bounded retries, idempotency and a documented safe-stop path.

rules.title: Execution context model
rules.requirement: Represent process, thread, interrupt, exception, task and bare-metal contexts with allowed operations.
rules.acceptance: Context checking rejects blocking, allocation or unsafe calls in restricted ISR/exception contexts.

rules.title: CPU affinity constraints
rules.requirement: Represent allowed CPU sets, core preferences and reversible thread-placement leases.
rules.acceptance: Planning is inert by default; live placement is limited to the calling process/thread and OS-granted CPU set.

rules.title: Scheduler semantics
rules.requirement: Separate modeled scheduling policy from real OS scheduling and privileged scheduler control.
rules.acceptance: Simulation is deterministic; live adapters identify the OS policy and do not claim kernel control without a driver/API.

rules.title: Interrupt-context restrictions
rules.requirement: Define interrupt-safe APIs, stack budgets, reentrancy, lock-free requirements and deferred-work handoff.
rules.acceptance: Static checks and target tests reject blocking/allocating calls in ISR-restricted functions.

rules.title: Typed clock sources
rules.requirement: Represent monotonic clocks, architectural counters and device timers with frequency, width, scope and unit.
rules.acceptance: Conversions require calibrated frequency and uncertainty; TSC ticks are never silently called core cycles.

rules.title: Cycle-accurate execution
rules.requirement: Provide a discrete-event CPU model that advances architectural and microarchitectural state per modeled cycle.
rules.acceptance: Reference traces reproduce instruction, memory and exception timelines for published model fixtures.

rules.title: Latency and jitter measurement
rules.requirement: Measure latency distributions with warm-up, sample count, clock source, workload, affinity and environmental metadata.
rules.acceptance: Reports include percentile, dispersion, outlier policy and evidence mode; they do not imply hard real-time guarantees.

rules.title: Concurrent interleaving model
rules.requirement: Explore multicore interleavings, synchronization order, cache visibility and data-race scenarios.
rules.acceptance: Bounded model-checking fixtures reproduce known races and verify declared synchronization eliminates them.

rules.title: Deterministic record and replay
rules.requirement: Record nondeterministic inputs, event order, clock mapping, device observations and execution checkpoints.
rules.acceptance: Replay either reproduces the recorded modeled execution or reports the first divergence with provenance.

rules.title: Power and thermal control
rules.requirement: Inspect energy, frequency, thermal and power states; expose writes only through vendor/OS-approved adapters.
rules.acceptance: Read-only mode is default; any control is board/model-specific, consented, reversible where possible and temperature-guarded.

rules.title: Transistor device models
rules.requirement: Represent MOSFET and other supported devices through explicit model parameters and validity domains.
rules.acceptance: The model exports a simulator-compatible netlist and passes reference operating-point fixtures.

rules.title: Electrical units and quantities
rules.requirement: Use dimensioned voltage, current, resistance, capacitance, charge and power values with explicit units.
rules.acceptance: The type system rejects dimensionally invalid formulas and conversions without unit scaling.

rules.title: Logic gate simulation
rules.requirement: Model primitive gates, propagation delay, drive constraints and unknown/high-impedance states where required.
rules.acceptance: Truth-table and timing fixtures match declared gate semantics, including X/Z behavior where supported.

rules.title: Combinational circuit synthesis
rules.requirement: Describe adders, muxes, decoders, comparators and arbitrary combinational networks.
rules.acceptance: Equivalence tests compare synthesized network outputs with a reference function across exhaustive or randomized inputs.

rules.title: Sequential circuit models
rules.requirement: Describe flip-flops, latches, counters, registers, finite-state machines and reset behavior.
rules.acceptance: Clocked simulation checks edge semantics, reset priority, setup/hold assumptions and state transitions.

rules.title: Clock-domain crossing
rules.requirement: Model asynchronous clock domains, synchronizers, metastability risk and CDC constraints.
rules.acceptance: CDC analysis flags unsynchronized crossings and records modeled probability/assumptions without claiming physical certainty.

rules.title: Static timing analysis
rules.requirement: Analyze path delay, setup/hold slack, clock uncertainty and timing exceptions for a declared library/model.
rules.acceptance: Timing reports include constraints, library identity and worst paths; unknown delay data prevents pass certification.

rules.title: Netlist graph representation
rules.requirement: Represent cells, pins, nets, drivers, loads, hierarchy and connectivity as a typed graph.
rules.acceptance: Graph validation rejects dangling pins, multiple illegal drivers and combinational loops where prohibited.

rules.title: RTL and synthesis flow
rules.requirement: Integrate synthesizable hardware-description subsets and external synthesis tools through explicit adapters.
rules.acceptance: A reproducible flow compiles RTL, records tool versions and checks synthesized structure against constraints.

rules.title: Physical design and sign-off
rules.requirement: Integrate floorplanning, placement, routing, parasitic extraction, DRC, LVS and PVT-corner analysis as external EDA stages.
rules.acceptance: A physical sign-off claim requires target process/library data and successful external tool reports; a software model alone is insufficient.

rules.title: Canonical Reaper frontend
rules.requirement: Keep accepted hardware-language syntax and normative grammar under Reaper ownership; Pytyliki supplies domain modules and target profiles.
rules.acceptance: A pinned Reaper toolchain parses the canonical source and emits versioned diagnostics; Pytyliki does not fork the grammar.

rules.title: Canonical typed IR and source mapping
rules.requirement: Use Reaper typed IR, Span and SourceMap as the source of truth for every hardware operation.
rules.acceptance: Every lowered instruction/effect maps to source Span and passes IR schema plus round-trip fixtures.

rules.title: Effect and capability IR
rules.requirement: Carry memory, MMIO, DMA, interrupt, timing, privilege and nondeterminism effects through the IR.
rules.acceptance: A denied capability or missing effect declaration is rejected before backend code generation.

rules.title: HIR/MIR/LIR lowering
rules.requirement: Lower high-level hardware descriptions through stable, inspectable intermediate representations.
rules.acceptance: Each pass has pre/postconditions, deterministic output and golden IR regression tests.

rules.title: ABI and calling-convention control
rules.requirement: Model DABI64 and target ABIs, register assignments, stack layout, aggregate passing and unwind boundaries.
rules.acceptance: Cross-language fixtures validate parameter/result layout and reject incompatible ABI revisions.

rules.title: Assembler and object writer
rules.requirement: Provide assembler, object sections, symbols, relocations and architecture-specific encoding backends.
rules.acceptance: Object fixtures are accepted by independent inspection tools and match golden bytes/relocations.

rules.title: Linker and loader path
rules.requirement: Develop deterministic linking, relocation application, image layout and a constrained loader interface.
rules.acceptance: Relocation fixtures resolve correctly; loader validates permissions, address ranges and target ABI before mapping.

rules.title: No-runtime and bare-metal profiles
rules.requirement: Support no_std/no_alloc, caller-owned storage, deterministic startup and explicit entry points.
rules.acceptance: Minimal artifacts link without an implicit runtime or allocator and pass target-specific startup tests.

rules.title: Cross-target code generation
rules.requirement: Select backend by ISA, ABI, feature set and execution environment without pretending all targets are equivalent.
rules.acceptance: A target matrix compiles shared conformance programs or emits a precise unsupported-feature diagnostic.

rules.title: Artifact inspection and reproducibility
rules.requirement: Inspect generated code, relocations, memory maps, dependency versions and deterministic build inputs.
rules.acceptance: Repeated builds from pinned inputs produce byte-identical outputs or explain nondeterministic sections.

rules.title: Static safety analysis
rules.requirement: Analyze types, bounds, lifetimes, register constraints, effects, privileges and concurrency before execution.
rules.acceptance: Negative fixtures are rejected with stable diagnostics and source spans.

rules.title: Proof-carrying compiler passes
rules.requirement: Attach machine-checkable proof obligations or validated invariants to semantics-preserving compiler transformations.
rules.acceptance: Proof checks run in CI for supported passes; unproved experimental passes remain explicitly marked.

rules.title: Reference and differential simulator
rules.requirement: Compare independent CPU/device models and supported reference implementations using identical input traces.
rules.acceptance: Differential mismatches are minimized and reported with model versions and deterministic seeds.

rules.title: Instruction-level simulator
rules.requirement: Interpret supported ISA instructions with architectural state, exceptions and memory effects.
rules.acceptance: Architecture conformance suites pass for every claimed instruction; missing instructions fail explicitly.

rules.title: Cycle-accurate simulator
rules.requirement: Simulate pipeline, caches, buses and timing per cycle for a declared model.
rules.acceptance: Cycle traces match golden model fixtures and never claim cycle fidelity for undocumented physical CPUs.

rules.title: Fault injection and trace verification
rules.requirement: Inject bounded faults in simulators and validate trace, recovery and safe-stop behavior.
rules.acceptance: Tests prove bounded execution and recovery decisions; live hardware fault injection requires separate lab authorization.

rules.title: Hardware-in-the-loop qualification
rules.requirement: Run target tests on named board, silicon revision, toolchain, firmware and test fixture.
rules.acceptance: Every qualification report records exact hardware identity and operator-approved procedure; host-only results cannot pass this gate.

rules.title: Golden conformance corpus
rules.requirement: Maintain golden source, IR, assembly, object, memory-map, trace and simulator outputs.
rules.acceptance: CI detects drift and requires reviewed fixture changes with provenance.

rules.title: Evidence provenance and trust
rules.requirement: Distinguish live measurement, OS-reported inventory, static analysis, fixture, simulation and physical sign-off evidence.
rules.acceptance: Every report includes evidence_mode, provider, target, timestamp/build identity and confidence limitations.

rules.title: Reproducible experiments
rules.requirement: Pin source revisions, tools, parameters, seeds, fixtures and result formats for experiments.
rules.acceptance: A clean environment can reproduce the declared output or reports the precise missing dependency.

rules.title: Capability-secured hardware access
rules.requirement: Require narrow, revocable capabilities for each privileged register, memory mapping, DMA queue and device operation.
rules.acceptance: Denied-by-default tests prove missing, expired or wrong-target capabilities cannot reach a hardware backend.

rules.title: Explicit unsafe contracts
rules.requirement: Mark unsafe regions and state preconditions, invariants, clobbers, lifetime and failure behavior.
rules.acceptance: Every unsafe API has reviewed safety documentation and positive/negative compile-time or runtime tests.

rules.title: OS and privilege boundary
rules.requirement: Keep process-level tools separate from kernel drivers, hypervisors, firmware and board startup code.
rules.acceptance: Unprivileged builds cannot silently elevate; privileged adapters are separate, signed/reviewed and target-specific.

rules.title: Local-first deterministic behavior
rules.requirement: Keep discovery and analysis local, bounded and read-only by default; network access is explicit and optional.
rules.acceptance: Offline tests pass; no hidden telemetry, downloads, tool installation or device modification occurs.

rules.title: Versioned architecture adapters
rules.requirement: Add ISA, OS, device and board adapters through stable versioned contracts and explicit capability declarations.
rules.acceptance: A new adapter passes contract tests and cannot broaden another platform's permissions.

rules.title: Language bridge registry
rules.requirement: Maintain the planned 66-language/toolchain registry with separate statuses for profile, parser, FFI, ABI, compiler and verification support.
rules.acceptance: Every registry entry has a unique identity and honest support level; a profile is never counted as a working compiler.

rules.title: Complete specifications and migration policy
rules.requirement: Document syntax, semantics, APIs, ABI compatibility, diagnostics, examples and deprecation rules.
rules.acceptance: Every public contract version has schema, changelog, examples and compatibility tests.

rules.title: Supply-chain and toolchain integrity
rules.requirement: Pin compiler/tool versions and hashes; validate imported packages, generated artifacts and signed release evidence.
rules.acceptance: CI verifies pins/digests and records provenance; untrusted binaries are never auto-executed.

rules.title: Per-target conformance matrix
rules.requirement: Maintain independent compile, simulation and hardware qualification status per ISA/OS/board combination.
rules.acceptance: Support claims are generated from test evidence and identify unsupported or unqualified combinations.

rules.title: Evidence-based lowest-level claim

safety_invariants: Host discovery and inspection are read-only by default.
A model, fixture, plan or simulation must never be labeled as live hardware evidence.
Physical, virtual, bus and MMIO addresses are distinct types and cannot be mixed implicitly.
Privileged writes require an exact target profile, narrow capability, explicit operation request and platform-approved backend.
Unsupported hardware semantics return an explicit unsupported result; they are never silently approximated.
DMA ownership, memory ordering, cache coherency and interrupt context are explicit contracts.
TSC ticks, device ticks and CPU core cycles are distinct units unless a calibrated conversion is supplied.
No CPU, OS, firmware, driver, voltage, clock or device state is modified by ordinary workstation inspection.
No hardware access is inferred from the presence of syntax, profile catalogue entries or simulator models.
Claims of lowest-level coverage are generated from rule statuses and evidence, not from marketing text.

low_level_contract.summary: Existing C11 target/memory/bus/IRQ contract. It defines versioned target descriptors, bounded non-overlapping memory maps, capability-separated RAM/MMIO callbacks, bus fences/audit, bounded clock/power requests and fixed-capacity IRQ registration. Tests use a fake backend; no physical target backend ships.
low_level_contract.reuse_policy: IRON and Omega-Null must reuse this target/capability/memory/bus/IRQ contract and extend it through reviewed adapters. Do not introduce a parallel target descriptor, MMIO permission model, IRQ registry or low-level rule catalogue.
